judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble's parenthetical defining "Manager" is garbled ("(“Managers Fund and Manager each being referred to..."), so the quotation marks do not close around the defined term and the words run together. That is a mechanical defect in the very sentence that creates a defined party term used throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The joint-and-several characterization matches Section 2.13 and the agency appointment in Section 16.11, so the parties' roles are coherent across the instrument. No operative provision contradicts the preamble's identification of Fund and Manager as Borrowers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line incorporation of the UCC definition; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.3 supplies the Article 9 tie-breaker and the "Code" definition supplies the jurisdiction, so the reference is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but conventional enumeration of who counts as an obligor; the terms used are themselves defined elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Notes Receivable machinery in Sections 4.3, 6.2 and the Eligible Notes Receivable definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard definitional language with an illustrative parenthetical; "related services" is mildly open-ended but bounded by the Bank Product Provider requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the Bank Product/Bank Product Obligations scheme in Sections 2.3(b) and 3.6 without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference definition with no substantive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4(c) does in fact create the term "Additional Documents," so the cross-reference is accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(a) creates the terms as stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to Section 16.11.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.11 appoints Manager as Administrative Borrower, matching this pointer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Control" is defined circularly as the power to direct management "whether through ownership of Stock, by contract, or otherwise," and the deemed-Affiliate rules apply only "for purposes of" two provisions, leaving reach contestable. The named term ("control") is genuinely open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Section 7.13 and clause (k) of Eligible Notes Receivable, and the 10% deeming rule expressly applies only there, which is a coherent though narrow carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure back-reference to the preamble.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble does define "Agreement," albeit in garbled OCR form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two fixed numerical margins tied to defined loan types; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 2.5(a) and 2.10(e), which invoke clause (b) of this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The premium is expressed arithmetically and drops to zero percent after the first anniversary, which is definite if odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7(b) requires payment of the premium "if applicable" on non-elective terminations, so after year one the drafted premium is nil, a tension a party could exploit but which harmonises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing catch-all, "together with any obligations undertaken or assumed relating thereto," is untethered and sits against two specific categories, raising an ejusdem generis question. "Approved Debt" also depends on the contested concept of a Permitted Reorganization.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Permitted Liens clause (c), Subordinated Debt, Section 7.1(e) and Section 7.10(b); the reorganization it contemplates is the transaction at the heart of this deal, so scope disputes are plausible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Approval standards are split between "not unreasonably withheld" and removal in Lender's "reasonable discretion," but each is a familiar, workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.21 supplies the list and Section 5.21 warrants it, so the definition is anchored.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(a) creates the term as stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (b) ("prepared by an appraiser and in a manner otherwise acceptable to Lender") and clause (c) (an "informal or unwritten estimate of value by Servicer") swallow the rigorous FIRREA standard in clause (a), so what qualifies as an appraisal is genuinely indeterminate. The disjunctive structure is exactly the kind a court must construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Section 3.1(t)(viii) and clause (r)(vii) of Eligible Notes Receivable and the reserve/valuation rights in Section 2.1(b), where a loose valuation standard sits awkwardly against Lender's valuation controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named individuals plus the sitting CFO of Manager; definite, though the names are OCR-corrupted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.2(a) and 2.8, which permit Lender to act on instructions of anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The amount that Borrowers are entitled to borrow" is defined by reference to sublimits and reserves rather than stated formulaically, leaving some circularity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Borrowing Base definition and Section 2.1(c)'s additional cash/unfunded-commitment cap, which are cumulative but not cross-referenced here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list introduced by "including," which Section 1.4 declares non-limiting, so the outer boundary of "financial accommodation" is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the Bank Product Obligations, Bank Product Reserve and payment waterfall provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple definitional pointer to agreements with a Bank Product Provider.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Bank Product Agreements are included in "Loan Documents" yet excepted from Section 15.1's amendment rule, a deliberate and coherent carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but standard sweep of obligations; the language is comprehensive rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Bank Product Obligations are carved out of interest accrual (2.5) and the Loan Account (2.9) but included in Obligations, which is consistently handled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition naming Wells Fargo and its Affiliates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Lender (Wells Fargo Foothill) is itself an Affiliate of Wells Fargo, which is workable but blurs the Lender/Bank Product Provider line in the Section 2.3(b) waterfall.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reserve amount is whatever Lender "has established" based on providers' "reasonable determination," a discretionary and open figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(b) says Lender will not establish reserves absent a Triggering Event, yet the Bank Product Reserve is a separate Borrowing Base deduction not obviously subject to that promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory reference; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the Insolvency Proceeding and Section 16.7 provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical rate definition with a conclusive-absent-manifest-error clause; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds the LIBOR Rate definition and Section 2.12 without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5(a),(d) and the Base Rate Loan definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition tied to the Base Rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 2.5 and 2.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Form-reference definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks ERISA statutory definitions with a six-year lookback; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.13 warrants no Benefit Plan, consistent with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sensibly extends the concept to managers and managing members of non-corporate entities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Section 3.1(c) and 6.3(d)(vi) consistently for LLC borrowers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but conventional collateral definition; the OCR interpolation of running headers does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Borrower Collateral clause (b) and the inspection rights in Section 4.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Each of and either of" is clumsy but its aggregating intent is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by Section 2.13's joint and several liability and Section 1.2's gloss that "Borrower" in financial covenants means Fund on a consolidated basis, which is a real interpretive overlay.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in grants "all property, including, without limitation," followed by twelve enumerated categories, so the enumeration cannot limit the grant yet invites expressio unius argument. The catch-all in clause (k) (assets coming into Lender's possession) is also open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the "Collateral" definition and Section 4.1's grant, which are consistent; the release provisions in Section 4.9 carve back in a coordinated way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Procedures are an extrinsic document "in the form delivered to Lender," amendable only with Lender's sole-discretion consent, so content is not ascertainable from the instrument itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: They are the yardstick for Eligible Notes Receivable clauses (b),(d),(e), Section 4.8 servicing and Section 7.9, so any dispute about their content radiates across the agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivially simple definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1 and 2.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear arithmetic formula: 20% of Net Eligible Notes Receivable less specified reserves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Sections 2.1(a)-(c) and the reserve limitation in 2.1(b), but the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount it supports cannot coexist with the 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio ceiling in Section 7.16(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Form-reference definition with a content requirement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B-2 is left as "form to be provided by Lender," so the referenced form does not yet exist in the instrument, a modest gap given Sections 3.3(f) and 6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Objective calendar definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the notice and payment timing provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(b) and 2.6(e) prescribe the required terms, and Section 3.1(b)(i) makes delivery a condition, all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13(a)'s New York governing law, although Section 2.13(g)-(h) waives California anti-deficiency defenses under a New York-law contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Sections 6.9 and 7.15 consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All cash, checks, notes, instruments, and other items of payment" ends in a general catch-all after specifics, and whether sale proceeds of a Note Receivable are "Collections" is not stated. That is a classic ejusdem generis/scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(a)(ii) requires all Collections into a Cash Management Account while 2.6(a)(iii) separately requires sale and payoff proceeds to be routed there, implying sale proceeds may not be Collections at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 4.7, 2.6(d) and Schedule D-1's control agreement requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A Note Receivable is "Defaulted" if either Administrative Borrower or Lender "deems" it non-performing or non-collectible — a purely subjective, unilateral and undefined test that two parties would read very differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term drives the Section 7.17 financial covenant and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (j), so a subjective trigger controls objective default consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: That interacts with Section 7.9 (procedures cannot be changed without consent) and Section 7.17's delinquency ceiling, an area of real friction.
